accept.reason: Targets the data bottleneck of computer-use agents with an abundant, unused source: public screen-recorded tutorials; annotation cost is the stated bottleneck.
Large mined corpus: 39,000 videos, ~1.52M ReAct steps, ~26B tokens, with long trajectories (avg 39.25 steps vs 18.6 for AgentNet).
Stage-1 video pretraining gives a consistent OSWorld-Verified gain over the SFT-only model: three 20-step runs 13.57-14.68% vs 9.13-9.42%, non-overlapping (mean 14.13 vs 9.32, about 17 of 361 tasks).
AgentNetBench step SR improves 64.1 -> 69.3, with gains on 8 of 9 comparable action types.
Monotone data-scaling trend: 0/50/100% of video tokens give 64.1/68.1/69.3 (AgentNetBench) and 9.3/13.3/15.7 (OSWorld SR@50).
Disclosed transfer of VPT-style inverse-dynamics auto-labelling to desktop GUIs, with a two-stage design: prompt-free dense event detection, then per-segment action parameterization.
Detector evaluated on a held-out 23 h set with 20,282 events, per-type P/R/F1, with weak types reported honestly (press recall 0.08).
Pipeline is clearly organized with overview figures and formal task definitions for detection and parameterization.
Training hardware, batch size, iterations and wall-clock given for all three models; full inner-monologue prompt; ScreenFilter thresholds; frame-rate policy.
Promised open-source release of ScreenFilter and Video2Action.
Budget sensitivity: the video-pretrained model gains from 20 to 50 steps while the SFT-only model stays flat (9.27%).
Per-application and per-action breakdowns let readers see where gains come from (e.g., chrome 8 -> 13-15 solved).
Cheap filtering: ScreenFilter processes ~840 h of video per GPU-day and keeps 7,377 of 10,000 hours.
Limitations of the metadata classifier and residual label noise are acknowledged.

reject.reason: The SFT-only baseline skips Stage 1 entirely, so it lacks both ~26B tokens of extra training (~1,920 H100-hours) and the OSWorld-G grounding pairs added in Stage 1. No compute- or data-matched control isolates the contribution of the mined video actions.
reject.location: Sec. 2.3.1 'GUI Grounding Data'; Sec. 2.3.2 'Stage 1 training'; Fig. 6; Fig. 11
reject.fix: Add controls at equal Stage-1 tokens: (a) grounding pairs only, (b) human/synthetic trajectories, (c) video frames + ASR without mined actions; ~2k H100-h each.

reject.reason: No comparison with any external agent or alternative data source. Agents cited as trained on the same OpenCUA/AGUVIS data (OpenCUA, Aguvis, UI-TARS) are not reported, and neither are trajectory-synthesis baselines (AgentTrek, OS-Genesis) at equal tokens. The 15.8% cannot be placed against the state of the art at 7B.
reject.fix: Report published 7B agents under the same protocol and a synthetic-trajectory Stage-1 at equal tokens; ~1-2 weeks of compute.

reject.reason: Action parameterization (the source of click coordinates and typed text) is validated only by a lenient manual 'plausibly produce' judgment on 500 samples: overall 0.658, drag 0.366, press 0.362. It is not evaluated against the held-out OpenCUA logs, which do hold exact coordinates and text, and there is no end-to-end estimate of trajectory correctness.
reject.location: Sec. 2.2.2 'Because ground-truth object boxes are unavailable'; Sec. 3.2.2; Table 2
reject.fix: Evaluate on held-out OpenCUA clips with exact pointer/text labels (pixel error, exact-match text); audit ~200 full trajectories.

reject.reason: 'Millisecond-precision temporal localization' and 'high fidelity' are not supported. Clips are sampled at 4 fps with a 2-frame temporal patch (0.5 s granularity), a hit needs only 'any temporal overlap', and no boundary error is reported.
reject.location: Sec. 1 contributions bullet 2; Abstract; App. C; Sec. 3.2.1
reject.fix: Report boundary error (ms) or tIoU-thresholded AP, or remove the claim; low cost.

reject.reason: The test-time-scaling claim and its mechanism are overclaimed. The 50-step result is a single run; +1.65 pt over the 20-step mean is ~6 of 361 tasks, and only +1.10 pt over the best 20-step run, against a 1.11 pt spread across the three 20-step runs. 'Teaches the model to decompose complex tasks into subgoals' is never tested.
reject.location: Sec. 3.1.2; Sec. 4.2; Table 4; App. G 'For the 50-step budget, we perform a single run'
reject.fix: Run three 50-step (and 100-step) seeds for both models; analyze trajectories for recovery behaviour, or soften the wording.

reject.reason: The data-scaling claim of a 'clear relationship' rests on 3 points with a single run each, with no variance and no intermediate fractions.
reject.fix: Add 25%/75% points and repeated OSWorld runs; moderate compute.

reject.reason: Possible overlap between mined tutorials and evaluation tasks: OSWorld apps (LibreOffice, GIMP, Chrome, VLC, Thunderbird) are typical YouTube tutorial topics, and AgentNetBench comes from AgentNet, the OpenCUA corpus also used in Stage 2 and for IDM training. No decontamination or split statement.
reject.fix: Report title/ASR overlap with OSWorld task instructions and confirm AgentNetBench tasks are excluded from Stage-2 and IDM data; low cost.

reject.reason: No ablation of the pipeline's components: inner monologue (GPT-5), ScreenFilter, IDM label quality (e.g., noisier or cleaner labels), or action labels vs. raw interleaved frames. It is unknown which part produces the gain.
reject.fix: Ablate monologue, filtering and action labels at a reduced Stage-1 budget (e.g., 25% tokens); ~1-2k H100-h.

reject.reason: Several numerical inconsistencies (recomputed). Table 1: Preds sum to 16,298, not 17,298, and the text says recall 0.71 against 0.70 in the table. Table 2: 330/500 = 0.660, not 0.658, and 0.366 is not attainable with 22 samples. Table 4: the stage2 50-step run solves 33 tasks = 9.14%, but 9.27% is printed, and the bucket denominators sum to 359. Table 6 sums to 53,375, not 55,603. Table 8 counts sum to 1,560,464, not 1,547,092, with mouse move/drag shares printed as 0.1% (actual ~0.5/0.4%). Table 3 has identical moveTo and dragTo counts (32,840).

Key data details are unclear: how stage-1 video trajectories get a task goal or instruction; how 39,000 of 55,603 videos (7,377 h) were chosen. App. D says 'Our dense detector is trained on 512,000' clips in the action-identification section, App. D ends with a dangling 'We visualize the data sample in Figure', and Sec. 4.2 cites 'Figure 10' for the step distribution (Table 10).
reject.fix: Describe the stage-1 sample format and selection; fix the references; low cost.

reject.reason: No ethics or legal statement on scraping YouTube (terms of service, copyright), creator consent or PII in screen recordings. Typed-text extraction can capture credentials: the Fig. 9 training example types 'lilybloom123.'. 'license/PII checks' is only asserted in an appendix limitations line, and the release status of the data is unstated.
reject.location: App. H 'Limitations'; Fig. 9; App. A; Sec. 2.1
reject.fix: Add an ethics statement; describe the PII/credential scrubbing and licence filtering; state the data-release terms; low cost.

reject.reason: Optimizer, learning rate, warmup, sequence length, image resolution and coordinate normalization are not stated (the configs list only framework, hardware, batch and iterations). The release of the mined dataset is not committed (only the tools), and monologue generation depends on the closed GPT-5 Medium.
reject.location: Figs. 8, 11, 12; App. F; Sec. 2.2.3; Sec. 1 contributions bullet 4
reject.fix: Add full hyperparameters and commit to a dataset (or ID-list) release; low cost.

reject.reason: The core mechanism is VPT's inverse-dynamics auto-labelling transferred to GUIs, and tutorial mining for agents already exists (AgentTrek with text tutorials; Jang et al. 2025 video-to-dataset for mobile agents). The delta against Jang et al. gets one sentence. No literature search was run (no network).
reject.fix: Add a direct comparison (method and, ideally, data quality) with prior video/tutorial mining pipelines; moderate cost.

reject.reason: AgentNetBench is a single run on 100 tasks with no variance. 'Terminate' accuracy drops 0.588 -> 0.237 after video pretraining, which is not discussed, although the text calls the improvement 'consistent'.
reject.location: Table 5; Sec. 3.1.2; App. G 'AgentNet Bench summary'
reject.fix: Report variance; discuss the termination regression (likely because video trajectories lack explicit task ends); low cost.

reject.reason: Absolute performance is low (15.8% OSWorld-Verified). There is one base model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B), one scale and no RL stage, so there is no evidence the gain persists with stronger SFT data or larger models (contribution check Q4).
reject.fix: Repeat with a second base model or a stronger SFT mixture; substantial compute.

reject.reason: Manual evaluations are under-specified. The in-the-wild detector check uses 10 videos and reports '~70%' with no counts. Table 2 does not report the number of annotators, the agreement, or what 'blinded' means.
reject.fix: Report counts, annotator numbers and agreement; low cost.

reject.reason: Action taxonomy is inconsistent: Table 1 has 5 types, Table 3 12, Table 5 10 and Table 8 9. The mapping (e.g., key/press/hotkey, moveTo) is not given.
reject.fix: Give one taxonomy and the mapping; trivial cost.
